summary: Intermittent inflight I/O bursts from background snapshotter causing GPU scarcity and flaky autoscaler behavior for Dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Background snapshotting/backup job in the dedicated cluster for DataFlowAI is producing short, high-throughput inflight I/O bursts. During these bursts GPUs briefly become unavailable for inference attach operations which triggers the autoscaler to shrink and then rapidly re-expand. Net effect: repeated attach failures, transient allocation gaps, and user-visible P99 latency spikes and 503s for the customer's reserved pool.

Impact:
- Customer: DataFlowAI (dedicated) is seeing p99 generation latency jump from ~120ms to >3s intermittently, plus a 1-2% spike in 503 errors during windows.
- Business: Dedicated SLA exposure for this tenant; potential churn risk if sustained.

Timeline (local timestamps UTC):
- 2026-03-12 03:18: first alert from customer (support ticket).
- 2026-03-12 03:22: Support reproduced elevated p99 in prod-us-west-2 and escalated to SRE.
- 2026-03-12 03:40: SRE observed short (~5-20s) NVMe/io wait spikes on nodes hosting the dedicated pool; correlated with snapshotter throughput peaks.
- 2026-03-12 04:05: Autoscaler recorded rapid shrink (release of GPU slots) followed by re-attach attempts; several attach RPCs timed out.
- 2026-03-12 08:00: Temporary mitigation applied (throttle background snapshot bandwidth for tenant namespace).

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated cluster: prod-us-west-2 reserved pool id: dp-84a9
- Infra: A100 nodes with NVMe-backed local scratch and periodic background snapshotter that flushes to S3
- Customer routes: dedicated reserved model routes pinned to rwkv-14b-quant and gptx-4b variants

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Run production traffic (typical mix of short chat streams + generation).
2) Background snapshotter initiates shard checkpoint flush; observed sustained NVMe write IOPS surge for 5-20s.
3) During the burst, serving runtime reports elevated io_wait%, attach latency increases; autoscaler interprets reduced attach success and triggers shrink.
4) When burst subsides, kube/gpu attach succeeds and autoscaler grows back, causing brief rebalancing and more attach traffic.

Observables & logs:
- Metrics: node.io.wait p95 spikes to 3800ms; gpu_attach_latency p99 increases to >2s; reserved_pool_alloc_failures increased by 8x during windows.
- Kube logs: repeated errors similar to "device plugin: failed to allocate device: timeout attaching GPU" stamped during bursts.
- Snapshotter logs (node agent): "flushing checkpoint shard=237 size=2.1GB duration=18s throughput=120MB/s"
- Autoscaler events: "pool dp-84a9: scaleDown triggered due to attach failures (reason: attach-timeout)"

Investigation notes so far:
- Correlation between snapshotter bandwidth and attach failures is consistent across three independent nodes.
- Noise is tenant-local: other dedicated pools on same cluster did not show same severity; investigation shows DataFlowAI's checkpoint cadence is synchronized across many small shards (many >1GB writes concurrently).
- Hypothesis: high concurrent local NVMe writes cause elevated IO wait and block device hotpaths used by GPU driver or device-plugin, which increases attach RPC latency and causes ephemeral allocation shortfalls.
- Another contributing factor: autoscaler currently uses attach success rate as an input signal and has a conservative cooldown (10m) and rapid shrink policy which amplifies the oscillation when attach telemetry is noisy.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Throttled snapshotter bandwidth for customer namespace to 20MB/s per shard (temporary).
- Blacklisted the snapshotter process from sharing the same NVMe stripes as the GPU device plugin on affected nodes via IO niceness and cgroup IO weight adjustments.
- Raised autoscaler attach-timeout from 5s to 12s for dp-84a9 (short-term) to reduce false-positive shrink decisions.

Proposed long-term actions:
- Run a quota on concurrent snapshot flushes per tenant (service-side control) and stagger checkpoint windows.
- Add a device-plugin health metric that excludes transient local io_wait spikes from immediate autoscaler shrink decisions (introduce smoothing window).
- Consider moving heavy snapshot flushing off local scratch to buffered streaming to S3 to avoid NVMe saturation.
- Update runbook: when you see bursty io + attach-timeouts, first throttle snapshotter and extend attach timeout before moving tenant.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can DataFlowAI adjust checkpoint cadence/config on their side? (Support asked customer for their snapshot schedule and retention settings).
- Should autoscaler be tuned cluster-wide or per-pool? Proposed: per-pool attach-timeout thresholds tied to observed baseline.
- Need SRE to review device-plugin trace to check whether GPU driver threads are blocked during NVMe saturation (assigned to Marco).

SLA notes:
- First response met within 30m. Customer-facing mitigation (throttling) applied within ~5 hours of first report. Engineering action item created for follow-up and permanent mitigations.

next_steps: (1) SRE to deliver device-plugin trace analysis and confirm blocking code paths (owner: Marco). (2) Runtime to implement per-pool attach-timeout config and smoothing on autoscaler input (owner: Sasha). (3) Product to add per-tenant snapshot concurrency quota and recommended checkpoint-stagger pattern with docs for customers (owner: Elena). (4) Post-mitigation run for 72h and confirm p99 stability, then close ticket.
notes: This ticket surfaces a common pattern where local NVMe IO noise from tenant-side background work can cascade into allocation oscillation. Long term mitigations will be platform-level (quota and smoothing) and customer guidance (stagger flushes).
